changelog.name: v2.1.0
changelog.body:
feat: codes can be kept as favorites with the star on result cards and the create page, or by swiping a history entry right
feat: favorites stay at the top of history, can be renamed, fold away when there are more than four, and are kept when history is cleared
feat: opening a favorite draws its code again, and tapping the code enlarges it for another phone to scan, with PDF417 turning as it grows
feat: up to four favorites can be added to the app shortcuts from the long press menu in history
feat: history entries can be deleted by swiping left, with undo, and a long press opens a menu of actions
feat: the create page keeps its actions in a floating toolbar and shares the code as an image to any app
feat: history and favorites are included in Android backup
fixed: messages on the create page appear above the keyboard instead of behind it
fixed: scan controls, hints, the camera permission panel and image results fit narrow screens and large fonts
fixed: a back gesture cancelled from history or the create page no longer leaves part of the camera visible and stops later back gestures from working

changelog.name: v2.0.2
changelog.body:
feat: QR codes that the quick read misses, such as small, tilted or blurred ones, get a deeper read at full resolution and a second decoder, wherever they are in view
feat: codes in view are reported together, so a QR code and a mini program code side by side both appear in the picker
feat: mini program codes that cannot be read join the picker beside the other codes, from the camera and from images
feat: the camera focuses and meters on a code that is not read yet, and zooms toward small codes of any kind
feat: small codes farther from the camera are found sooner
feat: images and screenshots are searched more thoroughly, finding mini program codes next to QR codes and small codes on full pages

changelog.name: v2.0.0
changelog.body:
breaking: the package name is now io.github.lcebot.ferryqr, as LSPosed modules expect, so 2.0.0 installs as a separate app

feat: read WeChat mini program codes, show their content and open them in WeChat
feat: optional LSPosed helper that hands scanned WeChat codes to WeChat's scanner directly, without aiming again or choosing between several codes; it only hooks Android camera APIs inside WeChat
feat: with the helper, result cards and history open WeChat codes in WeChat instead of asking for another scan
feat: mini program codes that are located but cannot be read are offered to WeChat, from the camera and from images
feat: open generated text in Alipay, and in WeChat with the helper
feat: WeChat and Alipay actions show the apps' own icons
feat: revised wording in English and Chinese

readme:
# FerryQR

FerryQR is a QR code scanner for Android. Point the camera at a code and FerryQR opens it in the matching app. If no app fits, it shows the content of the code, which you can copy, search or share.

[中文说明](README_zh.md)

## Install

FerryQR needs Android 11 or later on a 64-bit ARM (arm64-v8a) phone. Download the APK from the [Releases](../../releases) page and install it. The optional [LSPosed module](#lsposed-module) is enabled separately.

## Scan results

> When there are several codes, you can pick the one to open.

**Links:** If an app on your phone can open the link, the link opens in that app. Otherwise the address is shown and you can open it in your browser.

**Alipay codes:** Open directly in Alipay.

**WeChat codes:** WeChat does not accept scan results from other apps, so when the camera finds a WeChat code, FerryQR can only take you to the WeChat scanner, where you scan the code again; for a code in an image, the result card tells you to choose the image from the album in the WeChat scanner. With the [LSPosed module](#lsposed-module), the code opens directly in WeChat without another scan.

**WeChat mini program codes:** FerryQR reads the round mini program codes with three eye markers. Mini programs only open in WeChat: with the LSPosed module the code opens directly in WeChat; without it, the result card shows the code drawn again from its content: scan a code the camera found again in the WeChat scanner, and for a code in an image, choose the image from the scanner's album. The few mini program codes that cannot be read are still recognised by their shape, and a result card lets you decide whether to open them in WeChat; nothing is sent until you tap it.

**Wi-Fi:** Shows the network name and password. Most networks can be connected to directly.

**Wi-Fi Easy Connect:** Opens the system Wi-Fi Easy Connect setup when the phone supports it.

**Contacts and events:** Can be saved to your contacts or calendar.

**Passkeys:** Opens your installed password manager so you can use a saved passkey.

**eSIM activation codes:** Opens the eSIM setup on your phone. If your phone does not accept this, copy the activation code and add the eSIM from the SIM settings.

**Phone numbers, text messages, email addresses, map locations and app links:** Open in the matching app.

**Anything else:** Shown as text.

## LSPosed module

FerryQR is also an optional LSPosed module. After FerryQR takes you to the WeChat scanner, the module shows WeChat the code you just scanned in place of the camera image for a few seconds, so WeChat reads it at once, without aiming again or choosing between several codes. WeChat's viewfinder keeps showing the real camera.

To enable it:

1. In LSPosed, enable FerryQR with WeChat in its scope.
2. Restart WeChat.
3. Open FerryQR; the scanner screen confirms that the module is ready.

With the module:

- Result cards offer Open in WeChat in place of Scan again in WeChat and Open WeChat scanner.
- WeChat codes and mini program codes in history open directly in WeChat; without the module, they cannot be opened in WeChat from history.
- WeChat mini program codes open directly in WeChat.
- The create page can open its text in WeChat.

The module only hooks Android camera APIs inside the WeChat process, leaves WeChat's own code untouched, and accepts requests from FerryQR alone. Without LSPosed, FerryQR works as described above.

## History

The history button at the top right lists the codes you have scanned, grouped by day. Tap one to copy, open or share it again. Swipe an entry left to delete it, with an option to undo, or right to add it to or remove it from favorites. The clear button at the top of the history page removes every entry except favorites.

Codes you use often can be kept as favorites: tap the star on a result card or on the create page, or swipe right or long press an entry in history. Favorites stay at the top of the history page, can be renamed, and fold away when there are more than 4. Opening one draws the code again, and tapping it enlarges it for someone else to scan. From the long press menu, up to 4 favorites can also be added to the app shortcuts, which open when you long press the FerryQR icon.

## Creating codes

The create button at the top right turns text into a code. When it opens, it fills in text from the clipboard and shows the code right away, and the code updates as you edit the text. Besides regular QR codes you can choose Aztec, Data Matrix or PDF417. If the text is too long for the chosen type, a message below the text field says so. You can share the code as an image to any app, copy it to the clipboard, save it to Pictures/FerryQR, or add it to favorites. The text can also be opened directly in Alipay, and with the LSPosed module in WeChat as well.

## Tips

A code does not need to be in the middle of the picture. FerryQR reads it anywhere in view.

When a code is small or far away, FerryQR zooms in by itself. You can also pinch to zoom.

If a code still will not scan, tap the reset button to return to the default zoom and restart the camera.

In low light, use the flashlight button.

You can pick an image from your gallery to scan in FerryQR, share an image to FerryQR from another app, or open an image with FerryQR. A shared or opened image does not start the camera; its result pops up as a card, and when the image holds several codes you choose one at the top of the card.

You can add FerryQR as a Quick Settings tile to open it quickly.

## Privacy

FerryQR only asks for camera access and has no internet access. It never sends the content of a code to anyone other than the app you open it in. Without camera access, you can still scan codes in gallery images.

History stays on your phone. The create page reads the clipboard once, when it opens. The LSPosed module only talks to WeChat on the phone itself.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). FerryQR uses [zxing-cpp](https://github.com/zxing-cpp/zxing-cpp), [ZXing](https://github.com/zxing/zxing) and [WeChatQRCode](https://github.com/jenly1314/WeChatQRCode), all licensed under Apache 2.0.
